doc: RETENTION-1 (2026-11-16): every table the tick worker creates is listed here. A table with keep_days is pruned once a day by seed/worker/src/retention.js (rows whose time column is older than keep_days, at most max_rows_per_run per table per day); a table marked keep: state holds current state, not history, and is never pruned. test/plan-limits.test.mjs fails when a migration or the worker creates a table that is not listed. Lesson from the fleet this org was split from: its audit database reached 1,011 tables, 266 of them backup copies never removed, and append-only ledgers kept every row forever. Windows: criticality reads 14 days (seed/autonomy/criticality.json window_days); the trust ledger reads every outcome, so outcomes are kept a year.

free_tier_samples.reason: FREE-TIER-1: hourly account-wide usage samples; the tick reads the latest two hours

airouter_cache.reason: AI-ROUTER-1: cached model replies, pruned by core/airouter (7 days)

airouter_calls.reason: AI-ROUTER-1: one row per model call, pruned by core/airouter (30 days); integer-millisecond time column, so retention.js cannot prune it

airouter_stats.reason: AI-ROUTER-1: one row per kind and model, the routing memory

social_posted.reason: REACH-1: one row per post and channel; the publisher reads this week, the reach loop reads a year

_migrations.reason: which migrations have been applied; a record of schema state, never history to prune

hits.reason: pruned by seed/analytics/analytics.js (35 days raw, 2 days self-check rows)

analytics_meta.reason: analytics settings and the report cache

items.reason: the work queue and its dispositions (the no-silent-drop record)

claims.reason: live claims; released claims are deleted by the claim reaper

trust_ledger.reason: one row per surface and action class

handoffs.reason: one row per handed-off pull request

audit_log.reason: AUDIT-CHAIN-1: sealed into archive segments after 7 days by seed/worker/src/auditchain.js

audit_segments.reason: one row per sealed segment (about one a day): the index and hash chain of the archive
